anomalies.description: A large, sudden explosion originates at the base of a multi-story structure, producing a rapidly expanding fireball and dense plume of dark smoke and dust that engulfs the building within seconds.

A large, sustained explosion or detonation occurs at ground level in a desert environment, producing a rapidly expanding plume of dense gray and brown smoke/dust that obscures the initial blast point and rises vertically while spreading laterally over time.; A large, sustained explosion or detonation event producing massive dark smoke and dust plume, progressively revealing a multi-story test structure (likely a building mock-up) as the smoke clears. The initial frame (f0 at 12.0 s) shows peak smoke volume obscuring the structure; by f15 (19.5 s), the structure is largely visible with residual smoke/dust still settling. This is consistent with a controlled demolition or explosive test rather than accidental fire.

A large, sudden dust and smoke plume erupts from the left side of the structure, indicating a detonation or blast event at the start of the sequence.; Sustained violent structural disintegration and debris ejection following the initial blast; the building progressively collapses inward and outward with continuous dust generation, consistent with secondary explosions or progressive failure from a high-energy impact/explosion.

A sustained dust and debris cloud envelops a multi-story structure, indicating a recent or ongoing explosive event (e.g., controlled demolition or blast). The cloud expands and slowly dissipates over the interval, with no visible fire or secondary detonations, but consistent with post-blast dust propagation.
